annotator_prompt.name: target_locations
annotator_prompt.description: During initialization, the policy localized visible colored cubes differently because the rule specified cover geometry but not the cube landmark. During exchanges it sometimes substituted another target's stored coordinate for a measurement; after grasp closure it sometimes treated finger occlusion as preventing all localization. These cause PREDICTABILITY failures even where the next waypoint is within tolerance. Keep the ordered list of last reliably measured target central-axis [x,y] coordinates. Specify initialization from the center of each cube's horizontal top face at approximately z=0.03 m, using calibrated views rather than the whole silhouette or a table-plane projection. For covers, distinguish observed support from mere cessation of image motion: a visible lower boundary consistent with table contact and full-face geometry consistent with the resting cover height can establish support at an exchange endpoint; unchanged supported geometry can carry that evidence forward. Closure around a previously supported cover does not invalidate its resting height when the clip shows no lift or tipping. Visible opposing outer edges or reconstructible outer corners in the wrist view can then establish the center despite finger occlusion. Update an uncompleted entry when this measurement establishes displacement; retain it when measurements agree within visual uncertainty. For example, a pre-lift measurement may change [[0.021,-0.125],[0.025,0.043]] to [[0.019,-0.124],[0.025,0.043]]. Do not obtain an exchanged target's coordinate merely by copying a former occupant's stored location. Reaudit endpoint updates and anchor agreement together: if endpoint support or localization is unresolved, retain the last reliable coordinates and do not annotate a new localization anchor. Preserve the existing successful-lift freeze and causal identity-tracking requirements.

annotator_prompt.name: tracking_frame
annotator_prompt.description: At the first unchanged front frame after a reliable anchor, policies retained the old anchor as well as the new frame because the new frame lacked an independent wrist measurement. At grasp closure they retained the entire approach history although the current views constrained the still-supported cover. Annotated singleton anchors at exchange endpoints also require consistency with the target measurements, not merely a clear configuration. These are PREDICTABILITY failures. Keep the ordered trajectory list and latest synchronized-anchor compression rule, but explicitly allow a newly shown frame to inherit established localization and support when chronological comparison establishes unchanged target geometry and unambiguous correspondence. No new wrist image or changed coordinate is required. This inheritance requires positive visible continuity, not merely an absence of a reliable new measurement; it cannot bridge an exchange, an unresolved elevation change, or an invisible target. At a closed but not yet lifted grasp, combine the current wrist view's exposed outer geometry with front-view support and correspondence evidence; finger occlusion alone does not disqualify an anchor. Only remaining requested targets must qualify. For example, when E55 inherits a valid supported configuration and later frames show motion, write [E55,E71,E84]; when the current grasp frame independently qualifies for every remaining target, write [E287]. If an exchange endpoint's coordinates remain stale because localization is unresolved, retain the earlier anchor and intervening frames rather than compressing to that endpoint. Audit annotations for this consistency.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: target_locations
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Initialization failures arose from using an unspecified cube landmark; exchange failures arose from confusing identity arrival with metric localization; grasp-time failures arose from rejecting partially occluded but measurable geometry. These break PREDICTABILITY. Keep requested-order central-axis coordinates. Initialize each visible cube from its horizontal top-face center at approximately z=0.03 m, checking agreement between calibrated views where available; do not use the silhouette center or project the elevated face onto the table. For covers, establish resting height from visible table-contact boundaries and face geometry consistent with support, or carry forward previously established support through positively observed unchanged geometry. A clear top center, an accepted robot waypoint, or momentary stationarity alone is insufficient. Trace exchanges before measuring endpoints. Never substitute another entry's old coordinate simply because the tracked target appears to occupy its former region. After grasp closure, use continuity from the supported approach and the absence of observed lift or tipping to retain the resting-height interpretation. Inspect the wrist image for opposing outer edges or reconstructible outer corners, excluding the fingers and inset panels; partial occlusion does not prevent measurement when these constrain the center. Update uncompleted entries for resolved displacement, retain values when the measurement agrees within uncertainty, and freeze only after the successful lift is observed. For example, a grasp-time update can yield [[0.019,-0.124],[0.025,0.043]]. If support, correspondence, or center remains unresolved, retain the previous coordinate and preserve the trajectory needed to interpret it.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: tracking_frame
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Policies unnecessarily retained a preceding anchor when a new front frame showed the same reliably supported targets, and retained approach histories at closed grasps whose current views still localized all remaining targets. Conversely, a clear exchange endpoint must not become an anchor while its target coordinates remain unresolved. These are PREDICTABILITY failures. Append new labels chronologically, then test for the latest synchronized anchor. A new frame may inherit localization and support from the preceding reliable evidence when comparison of the retained frames and current clip positively establishes unchanged visible target geometry and correspondence. It need not have its own wrist view or produce different coordinates. Do not inherit through an intervening exchange, unresolved height change, or invisibility. Once targets move, use fresh reliable localization before making another anchor. At grasp closure, use the current wrist and front views together: still-supported height and exposed opposing outer geometry can qualify the grasped target despite fingers hiding part of it; other remaining targets must also be localized. Completed targets need not qualify. Thus an unchanged first frame followed by motion may produce [E55,E71,E84], while a sufficiently visible current grasp may produce [E287]. If no frame qualifies, retain the earlier anchor and the full subsequent trajectory. Never discard the trajectory merely because the endpoint looks settled or because a stale coordinate was carried unchanged.

proposal.refused: Do not add episode-specific coordinates, named-frame exceptions, or an action correction for these reports. The reported lift waypoints generally remained within the required positional tolerance, and the existing action rules already permit visual centering and require tracking before selection. The substantive failures concern memory predictability. Do not accept the claim that successful identity tracking alone permits swapping stored coordinate entries, nor the inconsistent combination of unresolved endpoint localization with a new singleton localization anchor. If localization truly remains unresolved, both the coordinates and the earlier trajectory evidence must be retained; if endpoint geometry establishes a fresh measurement, update the coordinates consistently before compressing. Likewise, do not declare every exchange endpoint supported merely because it resembles a prior arrangement, and do not declare every closed grasp measurable merely because the gripper has closed. The proposed support and partial-occlusion clarifications apply only when the currently available evidence satisfies them. Existing milestones and pickup-count semantics need no change.

fields.name: target_locations
fields.description: Read the requested colors in instruction order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cubes' central-axis world [x,y] coordinates. Project each cube's horizontal top-face center at approximately z=0.03 m using calibration, checking agreement between available calibrated views. Do not use the whole silhouette center or project the elevated face onto the table. Keep this requested order fixed. Match each descending cover to the cube underneath. Covering alone does not establish horizontal displacement: retain the cube coordinate unless reliable geometry establishes translation. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square from opposing outer edges and corners, and use the intersection of its diagonals as the central-axis landmark. Do not use a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or silhouette centroid. Project that landmark at approximately z=0.06 m only when available evidence establishes table support; do not project its elevated top onto the table plane. A visible lower boundary consistent with table contact together with outer-face geometry consistent with resting height can establish support. Carry established support forward only through positively observed unchanged supported geometry. Momentary stationarity alone does not establish support. After an exchange, establish support and localization afresh rather than inheriting them from the former configuration. A clear image center alone does not establish surface height. Update a measurement only when identity correspondence and surface height are both resolved. During grasping, visible opposing outer edges or reconstructible outer corners in the available calibrated views may constrain the center despite finger occlusion; otherwise carry the prior estimate. Closure alone does not invalidate resting height when visible continuity from the supported approach establishes no lift or tipping. Combine exposed wrist-view outer geometry with front-view support and correspondence evidence, excluding fingers and inset panels. Update an uncompleted entry only for resolved displacement; retain its value when the measurement agrees within visual uncertainty. Do not infer a center from the desired waypoint or treat every small pixel shift as translation. For an elevated cover, estimate elevation only when resolvable known-size face geometry or available simultaneous calibrated views actually establish it. Otherwise carry the last reliably localized coordinate rather than projecting onto the resting plane or guessing an elevation correction. Update when reliable geometry becomes visible again. Replay the ordered tracking_frame list followed by the current clip chronologically, removing duplicate labels, to trace each specific container before measuring its endpoint. The list's first frame anchors correspondence; later frames preserve motion that may not permit metric localization. target_locations contains last reliable measurements, not guaranteed current positions. Separate identity tracking from metric localization: a stale coordinate must not force a new identity assignment, and retained frames do not by themselves resolve genuinely ambiguous correspondence. At crossings, use continuous motion through intermediate frames, allowing horizontal and vertical image ranking to change; do not transfer identity by nearest previous position, initial slot, or final spatial order alone. Arrival in another target's former region does not justify copying that entry's stored coordinate: measure the tracked target using reliable geometry. If endpoint support, correspondence, or center remains unresolved, retain the last reliable coordinate and the earlier anchor with intervening trajectory frames rather than compressing to the endpoint. Compare successive front frames for residual translation, including during unrelated button motions: reaching a hand waypoint does not imply that covers have settled. First incorporate successful pickups observed this cycle into pickups_completed. Freeze entries at indices below that updated count at their incoming values; do not revise them during subsequent lift, lowering, or withdrawal observations. Update remaining entries after reliably localized translation, including movement during grasping. Preserve coordinates when images support stationarity rather than introducing estimation jitter. When localization is unreliable or temporarily occluded, carry the last reliable location without assuming the cover is stationary. Keep tracking later requested targets during button pressing and earlier pickups; use a newly exposed cube to confirm correspondence. Write coordinates to millimetre resolution without implying millimetre measurement accuracy. e.g. [[0.02, -0.18], [0.03, 0.13]]

fields.name: interaction_state
fields.description: Initialize start. Update from observed outcomes and the incoming milestone, not from the action you are about to choose. A completed approach above the robot-left button gives left_hover; its subsequent short close-only motion gives left_ready; descent to button contact gives left_pressed; upward withdrawal gives left_retracted. Apply the analogous right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted milestones at the robot-right button. In particular, arrival with already-closed fingers is still right_hover, not right_ready: the separate short closing action must be observed. Opening after right_retracted gives buttons_finished. Arrival above the next requested container at about 0.20 m gives target_hover; descending and closing around it near 0.063 m gives target_grasped; lifting it clear near 0.20 m gives target_lifted; lowering and opening near 0.07 m gives target_released; withdrawing the empty hand near 0.15 m gives target_cleared. A subsequent approach to the next target returns to target_hover. Retain the incoming state if the expected outcome has not occurred or no control steps executed. e.g. "right_ready"
fields.annotation: Observed interaction milestone, initially start. Button milestones are left_hover, left_ready, left_pressed, left_retracted, right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted, buttons_finished. Hover means the initial approach to that button has finished; ready means the subsequent short closing action has finished, even if the fingers were already closed on arrival. Pressed means the closed hand has descended into button contact; retracted means it has subsequently risen to approximately 0.15 m. buttons_finished means the hand has subsequently opened above the right button. Container milestones are target_hover, target_grasped, target_lifted, target_released, target_cleared. They respectively mean arrival at the selected container's 0.20 m approach, closure around it near 0.063 m, successful lift near 0.20 m, lowering and opening near 0.07 m, and empty-hand withdrawal near 0.15 m. Change only when the corresponding motion outcome is observed, never when its waypoint is selected. e.g. "right_ready"

fields.name: pickups_completed
fields.description: Initialize zero. Increment only when the incoming state is target_grasped and the current clip shows the held requested container successfully raised clear to about 0.20 m, ordinarily revealing its colored cube. Carry the count unchanged in every other situation, including further views of that same held container. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers successfully lifted in instruction order. Initialize to zero. Increment once when a newly grasped requested container is visibly raised off the table to approximately 0.20 m, exposing its cube. Do not increment for grasp closure, release, withdrawal, or repeated observations of the same lift. e.g. 1

texts.action:
Use the incoming memory together with outcomes visible this cycle to determine the current milestone; write those observations for the next cycle. Begin by locating both buttons and all requested colored cubes. Robot-left is larger world y, appearing on the right of the front image. Estimate geometry with the calibrated cameras, intersecting image rays with the appropriate object surface height rather than treating elevated tops as table points. Use wrist imagery to refine alignment. Do not reuse episode-specific coordinates.

Button rules: Independently localize each button using the center of its circular press surface, intersecting its calibrated image ray with approximately z=0.025 m. Do not use the square base centroid, a table-plane projection, the other button's x coordinate, or the achieved TCP position as its center. Prefer the current calibrated wrist view when the circle is visible. At hover and ready milestones, recompute the button center and command its x,y even if the preceding approach was accepted as complete or the closing action produced little motion. Hover tolerance establishes the milestone, not exact lateral alignment. All references below to the button center mean this visually localized center. From start, approach the robot-left button center at z=0.15 m, orientation [-3.1416,0,0], gripper open. At left_hover, command closure above the same center at z=0.15. At left_ready, descend over that center to commanded z=0.0075, closed. Actual contact may stop the TCP near z=0.024; this counts as contact, not a reason to press deeper. At left_pressed, retract over the localized left-button center to z=0.15 closed. At left_retracted, approach the robot-right button center at z=0.15 with an open command. At right_hover, perform the separate short closing action above the button even when the reported fingers are already closed. At right_ready, descend to z=0.0075 closed. At right_pressed, retract over the localized right-button center to z=0.15 closed. At right_retracted, open above the same button. Continue observing and tracking container exchanges throughout all these motions. Neither a return to the original spatial arrangement nor an unchanged shell appearance resets its hidden color association.

Container rules: Replay the retained tracking_frame list followed by the current clip chronologically to establish correspondence. target_locations stores last reliable measurements, not necessarily current positions. After buttons_finished or at target_cleared, select the requested target at index pickups_completed using its tracked identity, never the nearest cover to a stale coordinate. Before approaching or grasping, require unambiguous identity and reliable current localization. If ongoing motion or temporary occlusion prevents localization, use the existing purposeful settling wait or safe revealing withdrawal and reassess; do not assume waiting resolves a genuinely ambiguous completed exchange. Approach the resolved current center at z=0.20, open, pointing straight down. Choose yaw from its visible square edges so the fingers grasp opposing sides; use an equivalent square-symmetry orientation near zero where possible. At target_hover, descend to the container center at z=0.0633–0.0634 and close. At target_grasped, raise to z=0.20 closed, keeping the grasp orientation and approximately the container center's x,y; a small visual centering correction is appropriate. Fingers stopped around 0.018 m each and a container between them support a successful grasp.

At target_lifted, if more requested pickups remain, lower the held container using current TCP x,y to z=0.07 and open, preserving current orientation. Use current visible held-object geometry, not the frozen completed entry, to check placement. At target_released, withdraw vertically at current TCP x,y and orientation with open fingers to approximately z=0.149 before moving laterally to the next target. The completed pickup remains completed even though its cube is covered again. After lifting the final requested container, retain the grasp for automatic success; do not initiate an unnecessary release.

Never issue an exactly identical TCP pose merely to change the gripper. Apply this check only after correcting the nominal close/open waypoint's x,y from visual localization. If the corrected nominal waypoint is still within 2 mm of the current pose, add a small vertical displacement of about 3 mm while retaining the required gripper command. Do not add that offset when lateral correction already makes the waypoint nonidentical. Allow normal motion error when recognizing arrival; do not require exact equality.

If an expected motion did not execute, retain memory milestones and retry with a reachable, nonidentical waypoint. If alignment or grasp is visibly unsuccessful, correct using the current wrist image instead of advancing progress. If a target is temporarily occluded, first withdraw safely to reveal it. If containers are still moving and correspondence needs another observation, a short purposeful wait of 8 control steps may be used to finish tracking before a grasp. Do not guess a hidden color from its original slot, and do not wait without a specific visibility or settling purpose.
